hero.headline: South Korean Chipmaker SK Hynix Raises $26.5 Billion in Record US Listing
hero.body:
SK Hynix raised $26.5 billion in a share sale that marks the largest debut by a foreign company on US markets. The South Korean memory chip manufacturer's shares are set to begin trading on the Nasdaq, representing a major test of investor appetite for companies tied to artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The listing comes as chip stocks have experienced volatility, with semiconductor shares retreating from recent rally highs. Stock futures traded mixed ahead of the debut, reflecting investor caution about valuations in the AI-driven chip sector. The offering's size surpasses previous records for foreign company listings in the United States.

SK Hynix produces memory chips used in data centers and AI computing systems, positioning the company at the center of the technology industry's infrastructure buildout. The company's advisors are expected to earn substantial fees from the transaction, following a more modest payday from a recent SpaceX listing.

The debut takes place against a backdrop of global market movements driven by chip stocks. Semiconductor companies have boosted markets worldwide in recent sessions, though the sector has shown signs of pulling back from peak levels. Leveraged investment positions on SK Hynix are expected to multiply following the US market debut.

The listing provides a significant data point for how US investors value companies in the memory chip sector, particularly those supplying components for AI applications. The reception of the offering will likely influence other foreign technology companies considering US market listings in the coming months.

cards.headline: Israel shares intelligence on Iranian plot to kill Trump
cards.teaser: Israeli officials recently warned the U.S. about what they described as a new assassination threat against President Trump from Iran.
cards.body:
Israel shared intelligence with the United States indicating a new plot by Iran to assassinate President Trump, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing people familiar with the matter. Israeli officials characterized the intelligence as showing a fresh threat against the president.

The intelligence sharing comes amid ongoing tensions between Iran and the United States. Israeli officials presented the information to U.S. counterparts as part of ongoing security cooperation between the two countries. The nature and specifics of the alleged plot were not detailed in the report.

cards.headline: Ukrainian Drones Strike Russian Oil Infrastructure Near Crimea
cards.teaser: Ukraine has escalated attacks on oil tankers and refineries as fuel shortages affect Russian operations.
cards.body:
Ukrainian forces have escalated attacks on Russian fuel supplies, striking oil tankers and refineries with drone strikes described as operating at industrial scale. The campaign targets ships near Crimea and petroleum facilities across Russian territory, causing fires at multiple strategic sites. Russia has responded by banning diesel exports as fuel shortages begin to affect domestic supply.

The attacks represent Ukraine's strategy to disrupt Russian logistics and military operations by choking off supply routes into and out of occupied Crimea. Successful strikes on oil tankers in waters near the peninsula and refineries deep inside Russian territory demonstrate the expanding reach of Ukrainian drone capabilities.

cards.headline: Israeli forces expand control zone in Gaza as ceasefire frays
cards.teaser: Israel has pushed deeper into Gaza beyond areas controlled when a ceasefire was brokered, resulting in Palestinian casualties.
cards.body:
When the United States brokered a ceasefire agreement last year, Israeli forces controlled half of Gaza. Since then, Israeli military operations have extended into additional territory beyond the original ceasefire boundaries.

Palestinians living in the newly controlled areas face shelling at night and gunfire during daylight hours. The expansion of Israeli military presence has resulted in casualties among residents in these zones.

cards.headline: Trump removes all remaining members of Election Assistance Commission
cards.body:
President Trump has terminated all remaining members of the independent federal commission responsible for assisting election administration officials across the country, just months before the midterm elections. The action has prompted sharp criticism from Democrats and voting rights advocates who warn it could create chaos in election operations.

The three remaining commissioners of the four-member bipartisan Election Assistance Commission were removed on Thursday through different methods. The sole Republican appointee resigned, while the two Democratic appointees received termination notices via email from the White House presidential personnel office. "On behalf of President Donald J Trump, I am writing to inform you that your position as Commissioner of the Election Assistance Commission is terminated, effective immediately," the email stated.

The Election Assistance Commission serves critical functions in U.S. elections. It operates as a national clearinghouse for election administration information, accredits testing laboratories, certifies voting systems, and maintains the national mail-voter registration form established under the National Voter Registration Act of 1993.

The removals follow Trump administration efforts to change vote-by-mail requirements and ongoing investigations into the 2020 election outcome. Trump has previously made unsubstantiated claims about the integrity of mail voting despite losing the 2020 presidential election to Democrat Joe Biden.

Election officials quickly condemned the move. Adrian Fontes, Arizona secretary of state, called the decision "irresponsible and dangerous," stating that it "remains dead set on causing chaos for our election officials across this country" and "undermines the integrity of nonpartisan election administration."

The timing of the terminations has intensified concerns about the agency's ability to function during a critical election period. States typically rely on the Election Assistance Commission for support and resources as they prepare for midterm voting. The sudden leadership vacuum raises questions about how the agency will carry out its statutory responsibilities, including distributing federal grants to states and providing technical guidance to election officials.

According to the Help America Vote Act of 2002, which established the commission, the president holds the power to appoint replacements. However, it remains unclear how Trump plans to proceed with filling these positions or whether he intends to do so quickly enough to maintain the commission's operations before the midterms.

Federal agencies typically maintain leadership continuity during transitions to ensure ongoing operations, particularly those involved in election administration. The absence of confirmed commissioners could hamper the Election Assistance Commission's ability to certify voting equipment and provide technical assistance to states preparing for voters to cast ballots.

The White House did not immediately respond to requests for comment about the rationale behind the removals or its plans for reconstituting the commission's leadership.

cards.headline: Trump uses 'communist' messaging as economic concerns drive Democratic strategy
cards.teaser: President Trump has returned to calling opponents communists, a line of attack he previously used against Kamala Harris during the last election.
cards.body:
President Trump has revived "communist" framing as a key attack against Democrats. During the previous election, when he struggled to develop effective criticism of Kamala Harris, he eventually settled on calling her "Comrade Kamala."

This messaging strategy seeks to characterize Democratic policies as extreme, particularly on economic matters. The approach comes as economic anxiety shapes Democratic campaign strategy heading into elections.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise Above Prewar Levels After Shipping Disruptions
cards.teaser: Attacks on commercial vessels in a key strait pushed crude prices higher this week.
cards.body:
Oil prices climbed back above levels seen before recent military action, driven by attacks on three commercial ships in a strategic shipping strait. The disruptions to maritime traffic have affected crude supply routes, leading traders to price in additional risk premiums.

The latest hostilities in the waterway have created uncertainty about the reliability of oil transport through the region. Crude prices have wobbled throughout the week as markets assess the potential for prolonged shipping interruptions and their impact on global supply chains.

hero.headline: Typhoon Bavi Bears Down on East Asia as Landslides Kill 15 in Philippines
hero.body:
East Asia is preparing for Typhoon Bavi, a 1,000-kilometer-wide storm forecast to be among the strongest in decades. The typhoon is heading toward Taiwan and southeastern China after triggering deadly landslides in the Philippines that have killed at least 15 people. Authorities across the region have begun evacuation preparations and issued emergency warnings as the massive storm system advances.

Bavi's enormous size and projected intensity have raised concerns among meteorologists tracking the storm. The typhoon has already demonstrated its destructive power in the Philippines, where torrential rains loosened hillsides and triggered the fatal landslides. Emergency response teams are working to account for additional casualties and provide aid to affected communities.

Taiwan and coastal provinces in southeastern China are now directly in Bavi's projected path. Government agencies in both areas have activated emergency response protocols. Residents in vulnerable coastal regions are being urged to secure property, stock emergency supplies, and prepare for potential evacuations. Transportation networks, including airports and rail lines, are expected to face significant disruptions as the storm approaches.

The timing of Bavi comes during an already active typhoon season in the western Pacific. The region has experienced several severe weather events in recent months, straining emergency response resources and infrastructure. Climate scientists have noted that warming ocean temperatures in the Pacific have contributed to more intense tropical cyclones, though each storm system develops under unique conditions.

Authorities in Taiwan have begun deploying military personnel to assist with storm preparations, while Chinese officials have ordered fishing vessels to return to port. The storm's wide diameter means that even areas not directly in its center could experience hurricane-force winds and flooding. Weather services are continuing to track Bavi's movement and are expected to provide updated forecasts as the typhoon approaches landfall in the coming days.

cards.headline: Wildfire Kills 11 in Southern Spain as Heat Wave Elevates Fire Risk
cards.teaser: At least 11 people have died in a wildfire burning through Andalusia as authorities work to contain the blaze.
cards.body:
A fast-moving wildfire in southeastern Spain has killed at least 11 people, with 19 others missing. The blaze broke out near the village of Bédar in the Los Gallardos municipality of Almería. Victims died while attempting to flee the flames, and at least four of those killed are believed to be British.

Spain is experiencing its second heatwave of the summer, with soaring temperatures creating dangerous conditions for rapid fire spread. The wildfire has prompted a major containment operation involving emergency services across the Andalucía region, though strong winds threaten to complicate firefighting efforts.

cards.teaser: Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei did not appear at his father's funeral, creating uncertainty about his condition.

cards.headline: China Launches and Recovers Reusable Rocket in Space Race Milestone
cards.teaser: The successful recovery of the Long March 10B rocket marks a breakthrough for China's satellite industry.
cards.body:
China successfully launched and recovered its Long March 10B rocket, achieving a milestone in reusable launch technology. The achievement represents a step forward in China's competition with SpaceX in the commercial space sector. The successful recovery could significantly reduce launch costs for Chinese satellite companies seeking to deploy their own constellations.

Reusable rocket technology has been a key focus for Chinese aerospace engineers seeking to match capabilities developed by American companies. The Long March 10B's recovery demonstrates progress in landing and retrieval systems necessary for cost-effective space operations. Chinese satellite firms have been waiting for domestic alternatives to foreign launch providers.

cards.headline: Venezuela Earthquake Kills Youth Baseball Players
cards.teaser: Children from Venezuela's national youth baseball league have been killed or injured in recent earthquakes.
cards.body:
Earthquakes in Venezuela have killed and injured children who played for the country's youth baseball league, a program long considered a symbol of national pride. The league has begun counting casualties among its young players, with some children left orphaned by the disaster. Baseball holds significant cultural importance in Venezuela, which has produced numerous major league players.

The earthquakes struck areas where youth baseball programs operate, affecting facilities and communities connected to the sport. Emergency services are working to assess the full extent of casualties and provide assistance to affected families. The league represented an important pathway for young Venezuelans seeking opportunities through athletics.

cards.headline: Bayeux Tapestry Arrives at British Museum After Secret Transport
cards.teaser: The medieval tapestry traveled from France in a maximum-security nighttime operation.
cards.body:
The Bayeux Tapestry has arrived at the British Museum following a secret nighttime crossing from France, marking its first return to England in nearly 1,000 years. The medieval artifact, which depicts the Norman Conquest of 1066, was transported under maximum security to protect the fragile embroidered cloth during its Channel voyage.

The tapestry landed on Britain's south coast early Friday morning and will remain on loan at the British Museum for a year-long exhibition. Museum staff will now prepare the historic artefact for display, scheduled to open in September.

hero.headline: Witnesses say man killed by ICE agents in Houston did not ram officers
hero.body:
A Mexican immigrant who was fatally shot by Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents during a traffic stop in Houston this week was not the intended target of the operation, according to the Department of Homeland Security.

Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, who had lived in the United States for 35 years, was killed when ICE agents attempted to stop his vehicle in Houston's East End. The agents were reportedly seeking two people from Guatemala when they encountered Salgado Araujo instead, according to the New York Times.

Migrants who witnessed the shooting have provided accounts that contradict the official version of events. Witnesses stated that Salgado Araujo did not ram officers with his vehicle, challenging the narrative presented by federal authorities about what happened during the encounter.

New video footage has surfaced showing moments before the deadly confrontation, though full details about what the footage depicts have not been disclosed. The emergence of this video evidence comes as scrutiny of the incident intensifies.

ICE agents involved in the shooting were not wearing body cameras at the time, according to sources cited by Fox News. The absence of body camera footage has made it more difficult to establish a definitive account of the events that led to Salgado Araujo's death.

The shooting has drawn international attention and diplomatic response. Mexico is seeking prosecutions over the deaths of 17 Mexican nationals in the United States. The Houston incident appears to be connected to broader concerns about the treatment of Mexican citizens by American law enforcement.

The case raises significant questions about ICE enforcement procedures and accountability mechanisms. The lack of body camera documentation, combined with witness accounts that dispute the government's explanation, has intensified examination of the agency's operations and tactics.

The incident adds to ongoing national debates about immigration enforcement practices and the oversight of federal agents conducting operations in urban communities. The conflicting accounts between witnesses and authorities highlight the challenges in establishing transparency and accountability when federal agents are involved in use-of-force incidents.

cards.headline: FCC weighs ending school internet subsidy program
cards.teaser: The Federal Communications Commission is considering eliminating a program that reduces internet costs for schools nationwide.
cards.body:
Many schools across the country depend on a federal subsidy program that uses consumer fees to reduce internet costs. This funding mechanism has been critical for schools working to maintain student connectivity and access to online learning resources.

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr previously called for ending the program before his nomination by Donald Trump. The potential elimination raises questions about how schools would manage internet expenses going forward.

cards.headline: Waymo disables driverless taxi, alerts police after teens allegedly drink and fire toy guns
cards.teaser: The autonomous vehicle company remotely stopped a car carrying two 15-year-olds and contacted law enforcement.
cards.body:
Two teenagers were allegedly drinking alcohol and shooting toy guns inside a Waymo driverless taxi when the company remotely disabled the vehicle and notified police. The intervention allowed officers to respond to the moving car.

The incident raises questions about the surveillance and remote control capabilities that autonomous vehicle companies maintain over their fleets, and when companies should intervene in passenger behavior.

cards.headline: H-2A farm worker visa program faces reform debate despite growth
cards.teaser: Republicans in Congress are discussing expansion of the agricultural visa program while facing multiple obstacles.
cards.body:
The H-2A visa program for farm laborers continues to expand rapidly, yet Republicans on Capitol Hill are beginning discussions about how to further enlarge the program as part of broader immigration reform efforts. 

The expansion efforts face significant hurdles as lawmakers work to address agricultural labor needs while managing competing immigration policy concerns and worker protections.

cards.headline: Graham Platner drops Maine Senate bid after campaign turmoil
cards.teaser: The candidate has withdrawn from the Senate race, clearing the way for Democrats to select a new nominee.
cards.body:
Democrat Graham Platner has ended his U.S. Senate campaign in Maine following a sexual assault allegation against him. He has denied the accusation as "categorically false."

The withdrawal allows the Democratic Party to select a replacement candidate for the key Senate race. Platner's exit came after days of internal campaign turmoil as he attempted to remain in the contest before ultimately withdrawing.

cards.headline: Israeli forces expand control zone in Gaza as ceasefire frays
cards.teaser: Israel has pushed deeper into Gaza beyond areas controlled when a ceasefire was brokered, resulting in Palestinian casualties.
cards.body:
When the United States brokered a ceasefire agreement last year, Israeli forces controlled half of Gaza. Since then, Israeli military operations have extended into additional territory beyond the original ceasefire boundaries.

Palestinians living in the newly controlled areas face shelling at night and gunfire during daylight hours. The expansion of Israeli military presence has resulted in casualties among residents in these zones.

cards.headline: Britain's Ofcom proposes new rules requiring tech platforms to address scam advertisements
cards.teaser: The regulatory agency says more than half of UK adults have encountered potentially fraudulent ads online.
cards.body:
Ofcom has put forward proposals that would require major technology companies to take action against scam advertisements on their platforms. The regulatory body's research found that more than half of adults in the United Kingdom have come across potentially fraudulent ads while using online services.

The proposed rules would place responsibility on big tech firms to identify and remove deceptive advertising before it reaches users. Ofcom's action responds to the widespread exposure of UK internet users to fraudulent marketing content across various digital platforms.

cards.headline: Federal Reserve Chairman Appoints Marc Andreessen to AI and Work Advisory Role
cards.teaser: Fed chief selects venture capitalist and Trump ally to advise on how artificial intelligence is reshaping employment.
cards.body:
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh appointed venture capitalist Marc Andreessen to a task force examining how artificial intelligence is changing productivity and jobs. The new task force also includes former Walmart CEO Doug McMillon and Asha Sharma, who will co-lead the group alongside Andreessen.

The appointments reflect Warsh's focus on understanding AI's economic effects as the technology spreads across industries. Task force members share the Fed chairman's perspective on embracing artificial intelligence as a transformative economic force. Warsh also named members to separate monetary policy task forces as part of a broader advisory structure.

cards.headline: European Union Orders Meta to Change Instagram and Facebook Design
cards.teaser: European regulators say the social media company's platform features violate digital safety laws.
cards.body:
Updated Card:

The European Commission has accused Meta of violating the Digital Services Act through the "addictive design" of Instagram and Facebook. Features like infinite scroll and video autoplay contribute to compulsive use by shifting users' brains into "autopilot mode," regulators said.

Meta faces a potential fine of up to $12 billion and will likely be forced to redesign both platforms to comply with EU regulations. The company is accused of failing to adequately assess and address the mental and physical health risks posed by these design elements to users.

cards.headline: US Firm Apollo Acquires EasyJet in Surprise Takeover
cards.teaser: The European airline accepted a bid from Apollo that surpassed a previous offer from rival Castlelake.
cards.body:
EasyJet's board has backed a £5.7bn takeover offer from US private equity firm Apollo, valuing the airline at £7.15 per share. The all-cash bid emerged after the budget carrier had already accepted an offer from rival firm Castlelake, triggering a bidding war for the European airline.

The board said it was "minded to recommend" Apollo's proposal to shareholders, signalling its preference for the American firm's terms over Castlelake's competing offer.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Rise Above Prewar Levels After Shipping Disruptions
cards.teaser: Attacks on commercial vessels in a key strait pushed crude prices higher this week.
cards.body:
Oil prices climbed back above levels seen before recent military action, driven by attacks on three commercial ships in a strategic shipping strait. The disruptions to maritime traffic have affected crude supply routes, leading traders to price in additional risk premiums.

The latest hostilities in the waterway have created uncertainty about the reliability of oil transport through the region. Crude prices have wobbled throughout the week as markets assess the potential for prolonged shipping interruptions and their impact on global supply chains.

cards.headline: Hotel Workers in World Cup Host Cities Report Reduced Hours Despite Event
cards.teaser: Employees say they are struggling financially as hotel bookings lag behind expectations during the tournament.
cards.body:
Hotel workers in World Cup host cities anticipated increased work hours from the tournament, but have experienced disappointing results. Despite strong attendance at matches, hotel bookings have fallen short of industry projections, leaving hospitality employees with fewer shifts than they expected.

The disconnect between match attendance and overnight stays has created financial strain for workers. Hotels staffed up based on forecasts that didn't materialize, leaving employees with reduced income during what was supposed to be a lucrative period for the hospitality sector.

cards.headline: Barcelona Tourism Official Announces Plan to Limit Visitor Numbers
cards.teaser: The city's new sustainable tourism commissioner says his goal is to reduce the impact of 16 million annual visitors.
cards.body:
Barcelona's commissioner for sustainable tourism, Jos Antonio Donaire, stated his objective is to prevent any increase in the city's annual visitor count. The Catalan capital receives nearly 16 million tourists each year, and Donaire's role focuses on diminishing their impact on residents and infrastructure.

The commissioner outlined plans to manage tourism growth through measures aimed at controlling visitor volumes. The appointment reflects Barcelona's effort to address concerns about overtourism while maintaining the economic benefits the industry provides to the region.

hero.headline: OpenAI executive Fidji Simo steps down from leadership role
hero.body:
Fidji Simo, OpenAI's second-ranking executive, has stepped down from her full-time role after an extended medical leave. The departure creates a leadership gap as the company prepares for a possible initial public offering and works to compete with Anthropic in the enterprise artificial intelligence market.

Simo's medical leave lasted longer than the company anticipated. She held a senior position at OpenAI during a period of rapid growth and organizational change for the AI research company. Her role placed her among the top leadership responsible for guiding the company's strategic direction.

The timing of the departure adds complexity to OpenAI's current business objectives. The company is evaluating plans for a public stock offering, which would make it one of the most closely watched technology IPOs in recent years. At the same time, OpenAI faces increasing competition from Anthropic, a rival AI company that has gained traction with enterprise customers seeking AI tools for business applications.

OpenAI has not announced who will assume Simo's responsibilities or whether the company plans to fill the position permanently. The leadership change comes as the artificial intelligence industry continues to attract significant investment and scrutiny from regulators and the public.

The company's next steps in filling the leadership void will be closely watched by investors and industry observers. OpenAI's ability to maintain its competitive position while managing internal transitions will likely influence its valuation and market positioning ahead of any potential public offering.

cards.headline: OpenAI announces GPT 5.6 will power Microsoft Copilot 365
cards.teaser: The new AI model family will continue running Microsoft's workplace productivity applications.
cards.body:
OpenAI has designated GPT 5.6 as the preferred model for Microsoft Copilot 365, ensuring the new model family will continue powering Microsoft's workplace and productivity applications. The announcement reinforces the partnership between the two companies despite recent speculation about their future.

OpenAI received government approval for a public rollout of GPT 5.6 following an initial limited preview period restricted to government-approved organizations. CEO Sam Altman described the model as "the best model we have ever produced."

cards.headline: New investment funds launch excluding Elon Musk companies
cards.teaser: Two exchange-traded funds explicitly bar holdings in firms founded or led by Musk.
cards.body:
Two new exchange-traded funds have launched that exclude companies founded, controlled, or led by Elon Musk. The funds will not hold shares in Tesla, SpaceX, or other ventures under his leadership.

The ETFs provide investors a way to gain exposure to technology and automotive sectors while avoiding Musk's business empire. The funds reflect growing investor demand for portfolios that exclude specific executives or company leaders.

cards.headline: Google changes Android backup rules, counts data toward storage limits
cards.teaser: The company is rolling out local document backup while changing how backup data affects storage caps.
cards.body:
Google is rolling out local document backup functionality on Android devices while revising how backups count toward storage limits. The changes mean backup data will now contribute to users' storage quota, potentially causing those with multiple devices to reach Google's 15-gigabyte cap more quickly.

The update gives users greater control over their backups, including a new option to disable SMS and RCS message backups entirely. This flexibility allows people to manage which data gets backed up and how it affects their available storage space.

cards.headline: Vivo plans joint venture to expand smartphone manufacturing in India
cards.teaser: The partnership could establish a model for other Chinese phone makers in the country.
cards.body:
Vivo is establishing a joint venture in India to manufacture smartphones, marking a new phase in the country's mobile device production boom. The partnership follows Apple's significant manufacturing expansion in India in recent years.

The joint venture could serve as a template for other Chinese smartphone manufacturers seeking to build devices in India. India has become an increasingly important production hub for global phone makers looking to diversify manufacturing beyond China.

cards.headline: Over 1,000 Pokémon Go players gather in Times Square for Mewtwo event
cards.teaser: The gathering marked part of the game's 10th anniversary celebration.
cards.body:
More than 1,900 Pokémon Go players gathered in Times Square for a special event to battle Mewtwo as part of the game's 10th anniversary celebration. Organizers described it as one of the largest in-person Pokémon battles in history, with nearly 2,000 players participating simultaneously.

The event recreated elements from the original Pokémon Go trailer. Developer Niantic used the milestone anniversary to announce plans for future community-centered augmented reality gaming features.

cards.headline: Scientists collect tephra samples from Kilauea crater wall
cards.teaser: Researchers accessed previously unreachable volcanic material at the summit crater.
cards.body:
Scientists have collected tephra samples from the wall of the crater at Kilauea volcano's summit. The volcanic material had been inaccessible to researchers before the recent collection effort.

The summit crater has experienced 50 fountaining episodes, according to volcanic monitoring reports. The volcano remains under active scientific observation as researchers study eruptive patterns and volcanic deposits.

hero.headline: Filer takes first wicket in women's Test history at Lord's
hero.body:
Lauren Filer has entered the cricket record books after becoming the first bowler to claim a wicket in a women's Test match at Lord's Cricket Ground. The England fast bowler dismissed India's opening batter Shafali Verma for a duck on the opening morning of the one-off Test.

Verma's dismissal marked a significant moment for women's cricket, as Lord's hosted its inaugural women's Test match. The ground, which has been staging men's Test cricket since 1884, finally opened its doors to the women's format with this fixture between England and India.

Filer's dismissal of Verma came in the second over of the match. According to commentary, Filer delivered what was described as "a lovely delivery" that removed the Indian opener without her getting off the mark. The bowler, who fires deliveries at speeds exceeding 70 mph, followed up her breakthrough wicket with a less successful delivery, bowling a full toss in her next ball.

The achievement underscores a broader shift in women's cricket as it gains access to traditional venues previously dominated by the men's game. The decision to stage a women's Test at Lord's represents recognition that the format deserves equal prominence and facilities.

Women's Test cricket remains the least frequently played format in the women's game compared to limited-overs cricket. England and India are among the few nations that regularly compete in the longer format. Test cricket typically features lower scoring rates and extended periods of play compared to Twenty20 and one-day internationals, which have become the dominant forms of women's cricket.

India made a steady start despite losing Verma early. By the third over, India had reached 15 for 1, with batter Yastikaa making a more aggressive impression by scoring 11 runs. Yastikaa struck two boundaries off bowler Bell, one through square leg and another through backward point, suggesting India would recover from the early loss.

The match attracted growing support as play progressed through the morning. Early in the day, attendance was sparse, but spectators gradually filled the lower layers of the grandstand as the action developed. The pavilion became packed with observers keen to witness this historic moment for women's cricket.

England's focus on promoting women's Test cricket through hosting matches at cricket's most prestigious venue signals a commitment to developing the format. By providing access to Lord's, English cricket authorities have demonstrated that the women's game merits staging at the sport's most celebrated ground.

Filer's record-breaking wicket will be remembered as a landmark moment in the ongoing development of women's Test cricket, marking both her personal achievement and a wider milestone for gender equality in the sport.

cards.headline: Spain faces Belgium in World Cup quarterfinal
cards.teaser: Unbeaten Spain meets Belgium in a World Cup quarterfinal match as the tournament reaches the knockout rounds.
cards.body:
Spain enters the quarterfinal match unbeaten through the tournament, while Belgium aims to upset the streak with its collection of star players. Manager Luis de la Fuente has emphasized his team's identity and highlighted the role of young player Lamine Yamal as Spain prepares for the fixture.

Belgium striker Romelu Lukaku acknowledged the challenge ahead, stating his team must deliver a flawless performance to beat Spain. The winner will advance to the World Cup semifinals.

cards.headline: Djokovic and Sinner meet again in Wimbledon semifinal
cards.teaser: Novak Djokovic will face Jannik Sinner in the Wimbledon semifinals after both players advanced through contrasting paths.
cards.body:
Novak Djokovic and Jannik Sinner will meet again in the Wimbledon semi-finals. This rematch comes after the two players have followed contrasting paths through the grass-court tournament, with Sinner once again standing between Djokovic and his pursuit of history at the All England Club.

The winner will advance to the championship match at Wimbledon.

cards.headline: Haaland leads Norway to first World Cup since 1998
cards.teaser: Erling Haaland has guided Norway to World Cup qualification, ending a 28-year absence from the tournament.
cards.body:
Norway will compete in the World Cup for the first time since 1998 after Haaland helped the national team secure qualification. The striker, who was born in Leeds, England, but represents Norway internationally, has become a global figure while playing for a country with a population of 5.5 million.

Haaland's performances have lifted Norway back onto the international stage. The qualification marks a significant achievement for Norwegian soccer, which has struggled to reach major tournaments in recent decades.

cards.headline: Dybantsa outduels Peterson in Summer League debut
cards.teaser: AJ Dybantsa and Darryn Peterson faced off in their NBA Summer League debuts in Las Vegas.
cards.body:
Dybantsa came out ahead in the matchup between two top draft picks as the Wizards met the Jazz in Summer League play. The game marked the first professional competition for both players, who were among the highest selections in the NBA draft.

The Summer League provides rookies and young players an opportunity to gain experience and develop their skills before the regular season. Dybantsa's performance in his debut drew attention as scouts and team executives evaluated the new talent.

cards.headline: Fery reaches Wimbledon semifinal near childhood home
cards.teaser: Arthur Fery is one win away from the Wimbledon final after learning tennis near the tournament grounds.
cards.body:
Arthur Fery learned to play tennis just a mile from Wimbledon's Centre Court. The British wildcard has now reached the semifinals at the All England Club, bringing him one win away from the tournament final.

Fery's remarkable journey has taken him from his local courts to the main stage at SW19. His historic victory over Flavio Cobolli secured his place in the final four of the grass-court championship.

cards.headline: McGregor and Holloway face off ahead of UFC 329
cards.teaser: Conor McGregor removed Max Holloway's glasses during an intense face-off before their rematch at UFC 329.
cards.body:
Conor McGregor made his return to competition with an intense face-off against Max Holloway ahead of their UFC 329 rematch in Las Vegas on Saturday. During the confrontation, McGregor ripped off Holloway's glasses in a heated exchange. Fans welcomed McGregor back at the event.

The highly anticipated fight is generating significant interest on the secondary ticket market, making UFC 329 one of the most expensive mixed martial arts events in history.

hero.headline: Anthony Hopkins Signs Record Deal to Release Album of Original Compositions
hero.body:
Oscar-winning actor Anthony Hopkins has signed a recording contract with Decca Classics to release an album of original musical compositions titled Life Is a Dream. The album was conducted by Gustavo Dudamel, the Venezuelan maestro who serves as music director of the Los Angeles Philharmonic and Paris Opera.

The release marks a return to music for Hopkins, who has long harbored a passion for composition alongside his celebrated acting career. Hopkins has previously explored musical endeavors, though this represents his first major label album release with a premier classical music imprint. Decca Classics, part of Universal Music Group, specializes in classical recordings and has worked with renowned artists across orchestral, operatic, and contemporary classical genres.

Dudamel's involvement in the project brings significant artistic credibility to the recording. The conductor has earned international acclaim for his work with major orchestras and his commitment to making classical music accessible to broader audiences. His partnership with Hopkins on this recording suggests the compositions carry substantial musical ambition beyond a celebrity vanity project.

Hopkins, now 88, won Academy Awards for his performances in The Silence of the Lambs and The Father, establishing himself as one of the most respected actors of his generation. His move into recorded music reflects a broader trend of established artists exploring creative outlets beyond their primary fields later in their careers. The album title, Life Is a Dream, evokes both philosophical reflection and the dreamlike quality often associated with musical expression.

The announcement from Decca Classics did not include a specific release date for the album or details about the musical style of the compositions. Hopkins has not publicly discussed the inspiration behind the work or how long he has been developing these pieces. The collaboration between a Hollywood legend and one of classical music's most prominent contemporary conductors represents an unusual crossover that may attract attention from both film and music audiences.

cards.headline: Teddy Swims Releases New Single About Relationship Ending
cards.teaser: The singer dropped a new track inspired by his own breakup experience.
cards.body:
Teddy Swims released a new single titled Break Up in Reverse, drawing from personal heartbreak. The song reflects on the end of a romantic relationship that the artist experienced in his own life.

The track joins a catalog of emotionally driven music from Swims, whose soulful vocal style has earned him a following in the R&B and pop crossover space. The lovelorn composition continues his pattern of mining personal experience for songwriting material.

cards.headline: J.K. Simmons Says He Has Never Met Tom Holland Despite Two Spider-Man Films Together
cards.teaser: The actors appeared in two Marvel films together but never crossed paths on set.
cards.body:
J.K. Simmons revealed he has never met Tom Holland despite both actors appearing in two Spider-Man films. The pair shared the screen in Spider-Man: Far From Home in 2019 and Spider-Man: No Way Home in 2021.

Simmons reprised his role as J. Jonah Jameson in both films, while Holland starred as Peter Parker. The revelation highlights how modern filmmaking techniques, including separate shooting schedules and post-production editing, can keep actors from interacting even when they appear in the same scenes.

cards.headline: Jesse Tyler Ferguson to Play Truman Capote in London Production
cards.teaser: The Modern Family actor will reprise his role in Tru at the Menier Chocolate Factory.
cards.body:
Jesse Tyler Ferguson will perform as Truman Capote in a London production of Tru at the Menier Chocolate Factory. Rob Ashford directs the show, which opens September 27 after previews beginning September 19 and runs through November 14.

The production follows a well-received New York staging earlier this year. Jay Presson Allen wrote the play, which focuses on the author's life and work. Ferguson's casting marks his debut at the Menier Chocolate Factory venue.

cards.headline: Mediawan to Roll Out Game Show Trojan Horse Across Europe
cards.teaser: The French producer secured rights to adapt the Kinetic Content format.
cards.body:
French producer Mediawan has acquired option rights to adapt Trojan Horse, a game show format created by Kinetic Content, for European markets.

The rollout arrives during a surge in Greek mythology-focused entertainment, coinciding with Christopher Nolan's upcoming film adaptation of Homer's The Odyssey.

cards.headline: Fabiola Gianotti Higgs Boson Discovery to Get Biopic Treatment
cards.teaser: Italian physicist who led research into the God particle will be the subject of a feature film.
cards.body:
Italian physicist Fabiola Gianotti will be the subject of a feature film biopic titled The Mysterious Particle. Stefano Mordini, director of The Invisible Witness, will direct the project.

Gianotti led one of two experiments that resulted in the discovery of the Higgs boson, a subatomic particle nicknamed the God particle. The film is described as a high-end biopic focusing on her pioneering work in particle physics.

cards.headline: Malaysian Sci-Fi Film Mimpi Kita Secures Distribution Deal
cards.teaser: Abnormal Studios picked up theatrical and international sales rights for the fantasy feature.
cards.body:
Malaysian company Abnormal Studios acquired theatrical distribution rights for Malaysia and Brunei to Mimpi Kita: Castle in the Air, a science-fiction fantasy feature. The company will also handle worldwide international sales except for the two territories where it holds distribution rights.

The film recently participated in the NAFF Project Market's It Project strand at the Bucheon International Fantastic Film Festival. The acquisition represents a significant step for Malaysian genre filmmaking in the international market.

hero.headline: Trump removes all remaining members of Election Assistance Commission
hero.body:
President Trump has terminated all remaining members of the independent federal commission responsible for assisting election administration officials across the country, just months before the midterm elections. The action has prompted sharp criticism from Democrats and voting rights advocates who warn it could create chaos in election operations.

The three remaining commissioners of the four-member bipartisan Election Assistance Commission were removed on Thursday through different methods. The sole Republican appointee resigned, while the two Democratic appointees received termination notices via email from the White House presidential personnel office. "On behalf of President Donald J Trump, I am writing to inform you that your position as Commissioner of the Election Assistance Commission is terminated, effective immediately," the email stated.

The Election Assistance Commission serves critical functions in U.S. elections. It operates as a national clearinghouse for election administration information, accredits testing laboratories, certifies voting systems, and maintains the national mail-voter registration form established under the National Voter Registration Act of 1993.

The removals follow Trump administration efforts to change vote-by-mail requirements and ongoing investigations into the 2020 election outcome. Trump has previously made unsubstantiated claims about the integrity of mail voting despite losing the 2020 presidential election to Democrat Joe Biden.

Election officials quickly condemned the move. Adrian Fontes, Arizona secretary of state, called the decision "irresponsible and dangerous," stating that it "remains dead set on causing chaos for our election officials across this country" and "undermines the integrity of nonpartisan election administration."

The timing of the terminations has intensified concerns about the agency's ability to function during a critical election period. States typically rely on the Election Assistance Commission for support and resources as they prepare for midterm voting. The sudden leadership vacuum raises questions about how the agency will carry out its statutory responsibilities, including distributing federal grants to states and providing technical guidance to election officials.

According to the Help America Vote Act of 2002, which established the commission, the president holds the power to appoint replacements. However, it remains unclear how Trump plans to proceed with filling these positions or whether he intends to do so quickly enough to maintain the commission's operations before the midterms.

Federal agencies typically maintain leadership continuity during transitions to ensure ongoing operations, particularly those involved in election administration. The absence of confirmed commissioners could hamper the Election Assistance Commission's ability to certify voting equipment and provide technical assistance to states preparing for voters to cast ballots.

The White House did not immediately respond to requests for comment about the rationale behind the removals or its plans for reconstituting the commission's leadership.

cards.headline: Israel shares intelligence on Iranian plot to kill Trump
cards.teaser: Israeli officials recently warned the U.S. about what they described as a new assassination threat against President Trump from Iran.
cards.body:
Israel shared intelligence with the United States indicating a new plot by Iran to assassinate President Trump, according to a Wall Street Journal report citing people familiar with the matter. Israeli officials characterized the intelligence as showing a fresh threat against the president.

The intelligence sharing comes amid ongoing tensions between Iran and the United States. Israeli officials presented the information to U.S. counterparts as part of ongoing security cooperation between the two countries. The nature and specifics of the alleged plot were not detailed in the report.

cards.headline: Sen. Mitch McConnell hospitalized for nearly four weeks
cards.teaser: Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell has been hospitalized for almost a month with limited information provided about his condition.
cards.body:
Sen. Mitch McConnell has been hospitalized for nearly four weeks, with his office providing limited details about his condition or expected return. The extended absence marks the second time this year that a member of Congress has been away for weeks with minimal public information.

Calls for greater transparency about the health of elected officials have grown as McConnell's hospitalization continues. The lack of detailed updates has raised questions about how much information lawmakers should disclose when health issues prevent them from carrying out their duties. McConnell's office has not specified the reason for hospitalization or provided a timeline for his return to the Senate.

cards.headline: House Republicans frustrated as legislative agenda stalls
cards.teaser: Republicans express growing frustration over weeks of gridlock that have left them with few accomplishments to show voters before the August recess.
cards.body:
House Republicans are increasingly frustrated that weeks of legislative gridlock have stalled much of their agenda, leaving lawmakers with a limited list of accomplishments as they head toward the campaign trail. Hardliners have expressed anger over the stalled SAVE America Act and what they view as leadership's failure to advance border legislation.

The lack of progress has created tension within the Republican conference as members face pressure to demonstrate results to constituents. With the August recess approaching, the thin record of legislative achievements has become a growing concern for Republicans hoping to highlight their work during the midterm campaign season.

cards.headline: Democrats face setbacks in Senate races in Maine and Michigan
cards.teaser: Recent developments in two key battleground states have complicated Democratic efforts to retake control of the Senate.
cards.body:
Democratic chances of winning back the Senate have taken a hit following setbacks in Maine and Michigan, two states considered critical to their path to a majority. The collapse of Graham Platner's campaign in Maine has left Democrats scrambling to find a challenger to face GOP incumbent Sen. Susan Collins with less than four months until the election.

The twin setbacks in Maine and Michigan have forced Democrats to reassess their Senate strategy. Both states were viewed as essential pickup opportunities for Democrats seeking to flip the chamber. The party now faces the challenge of regaining momentum in these races while the clock runs down toward November.

cards.headline: Trump uses 'communist' messaging as economic concerns drive Democratic strategy
cards.teaser: President Trump has returned to calling opponents communists, a line of attack he previously used against Kamala Harris during the last election.
cards.body:
President Trump has revived "communist" framing as a key attack against Democrats. During the previous election, when he struggled to develop effective criticism of Kamala Harris, he eventually settled on calling her "Comrade Kamala."

This messaging strategy seeks to characterize Democratic policies as extreme, particularly on economic matters. The approach comes as economic anxiety shapes Democratic campaign strategy heading into elections.

cards.headline: Republicans begin talks on expanding farm labor visa program
cards.teaser: Republicans on Capitol Hill are discussing immigration reform focused on the H-2A visa program for agricultural workers.
cards.body:
Republicans on Capitol Hill are beginning discussions on expanding the H-2A visa program, which allows agricultural employers to hire temporary foreign workers. The program has experienced rapid growth and gained favor among farming operations struggling with labor shortages.

The H-2A expansion represents a rare area where Republicans see potential for bipartisan immigration reform. However, lawmakers face significant obstacles in reaching agreement on how to expand the program. Despite its popularity among agricultural employers, moving forward on these discussions remains challenging.
